Pair 1 was by far the closest. There, B's dated heavy grade, low-res road and empty highway let A's warm, modern lighting and denser Singapore streetscape compete, but A's errors and flat framing lost it. In pairs 2-4 the gap is large. B's frames are art-directed, dense, error-free shots with very strong car materials: environment reflections in the paint, chrome, glass lenses, detailed tyres. They also have readable foreground-to-background depth and supporting life (traffic, pedestrians, police car, jogger, neon, billboards). The A frames share good bones: a convincing tropical-Singapore identity (shophouses, HDB blocks, rain trees, yellow box junctions, local plates), pleasant warm sun and haze, and a clean HUD style. But they repeat the same faults. Motion blur ghosts pedestrians and bikes into see-through doubles and smears the median at moderate speeds. City spaces are nearly empty. The close-range cars have weak material fidelity and stray bloom sprites. The background towers in pair 4 look like blockouts. The minimap is a grey-grid placeholder, and the pistol ammo counter shows while driving. The fixes that would move A most are: 1) fix the motion-blur ghosting; 2) fill streets with traffic and pedestrians; 3) raise car paint, wheel and lens fidelity; 4) replace the blockout skyline; 5) choose camera angles and times of day that give the hero car rim light and reflections. B images that genuinely wow: pair 2 (dusk neon reflections) and pair 3 (hero-car materials). No A image wows.
